notes:
Summary: Ironbark is an enterprise SaaS vendor focused on regulated customers (healthcare and payments). Strong push for a Private VPC deployment with customer-owned KMS and strict egress controls. They view Redwood as a preferred partner vs building their own stack but need firm answers for network topology, static egress IPs, and audit export.

Key asks / requirements (from CTO & infra):
- Network: Prefer AWS PrivateLink endpoints + interface VPC endpoints to ensure no traffic traverses the public internet. If PrivateLink not possible for certain services, VPC peering is acceptable with strict routing rules.
- Firewall rules: Inbound only from private endpoints; customer will implement security-group + NACL rules blocking all other traffic. Need sample security-group and subnet port lists (we provided a starter diagram).
- Egress controls: They require that model inference requests and any telemetry not egress outside their region/project. Must support VPC egress policy that can be restricted to allowed Redwood egress IP ranges; they will add those to their outbound allowlist.
- IP allowlists: Customer demands a stable, published set of static egress IPs (or small CIDR blocks) for allowlisting. If dynamic, need SLA on change notification window (>=30 days preferred).
- Private DNS: Wants support for resolving Redwood service endpoints via Private DNS within their VPC (no public DNS resolution for inference endpoints).
- KMS integration: Mandatory customer-managed AWS KMS keys. Keys must be usable for request-level encryption; Redwood must provide guidance on key policy statements and cross-account grants. Customer prefers keys to remain in their account with no key material leaving their control.
- Audit logging: All request/response metadata (no PII payloads) exported to their CloudWatch/S3; retention policy 7 years. Need proof of concept for subscribing logs to their SIEM (SPLUNK) and for signed log delivery.
- Data residency: Primary requirement: inference and ephemeral caches must stay in Canada (ca-central-1). They will not accept multi-region replication outside Canada without explicit legal approval.
- Compliance docs: Requested SOC2 Type II evidence and ISO27001 letter; asked for a short onboarding checklist for security/compliance review.

Quotes from calls:
- CTO: "We cannot have any inference traffic egressing the public internet — PrivateLink or nothing."
- Head of Security: "We need the KMS key to live in our account and direct proof logs are delivered into our S3 with integrity checks."

PoC scope proposed:
- 2-week PoC in ca-central-1 within a customer sandbox VPC
- PrivateLink endpoint + route53 private DNS
- Customer-managed KMS for dataset encryption and key-use audit
- Log delivery to customer S3 + validation script
- Performance baseline: 99th pct latency under 200ms for 1-2 concurrent interactive chat sessions

Open items for Redwood engineering:
- Provide exact egress IP CIDRs and expected change policy
- Template AWS KMS key policy and example cross-account grant JSON (short-form)
- Network diagram variant for PrivateLink vs VPC peering (we gave one, they want a peering alternative)
- Clarify whether prefix/KV caching will store any fragments outside customer-controlled storage

Next steps (short):

- Deliver egress IP CIDR list + change SLA before review
- Legal: respond to data residency contract addendum by 2026-03-25
